title: Prompt-injection generalization: does one injection string compromise a homogeneous model fleet?

original_idea.body:
# Prompt-injection generalization

Test a bank of published prompt-injection payloads against 6-8 models in a simple tool-use scaffold; measure per-payload success and the fraction succeeding on ALL models (universal injections), relating universality to lineage. Public payloads + open models; no training.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — universal injections compromising agentic fleets is a concrete recognized security pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: published payloads + simple tool-use scaffold; the scaffold adds mild complexity, guided feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable (universal-injection rate) with the scaffold as a dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public payloads + open models, weak lab incentive, directly actionable for deployers.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on several models in a scaffold, light compute.

novelty.reasoning: Injection transfer plausibly studied; the fleet-universality-by-lineage framing may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Extends jailbreak-transfer findings to prompt injection; partly open angle.
